description.narrative: UNDP’s Governance Multi-Year Framework (MYF, 2020-2024) successfully contributed towards strengthening governance systems in Bhutan, providing key lessons for the next phase of UNDPs governance interventions. In response, a new Governance Offer has been crafted, aligning with Bhutan’s 13th Five-Year Plan and UNDP’s Global Governance for People and Planet (G4PP) framework.This portfolio is designed to promote a whole-of-government approach to strengthen governance and catalyze transformative change, especially byi. supporting economic transformation through improved public-sector capability and innovation; with a focus on establishing institutional structures for implementation of key national policies; and institutionalizing innovation across all public sector institutions to drive efficiency and effectiveness ii. Advancing Bhutan’s climate change governance, and the global climate change leadership role at , particularly through the G-Zero Initiative iii. Strengthening inclusion by enabling greater participation and equitable access for women, youth, and people living with disabilities; and iv. Improving governance systems and leveraging digital and AI solutions in core service sectors, specifically in the health sector, for health procurement, health investments, digital health solutions.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
